title: Attached tick
summary: Remove promptly with fine-tipped tweezers using steady upward pressure.
sources: 2024 American Heart Association and American Red Cross Guidelines for First Aid — Tick Bites
CDC — What to Do After a Tick Bite
actions: Use fine-tipped tweezers or a commercial tick-removal tool. Grasp the tick close to the skin at the mouthparts.
Pull upward with steady, even pressure. Do not twist or jerk.
If a small mouthpart remains and does not come out easily, do not dig into the skin; seek care if inflammation develops.
Clean hands and the bite area with soap and water or antiseptic. Record the date and likely exposure location.
Over the following weeks, seek medical advice for fever, rash, headache, weakness, or muscle or joint pain and mention the tick bite.
prohibitions: Do not burn the tick or use a hot object.
Do not cover it with oil, petroleum jelly, nail polish, alcohol, or cream.
Do not crush the tick with bare fingers.

emergencyCall.text: Emergency services are not usually needed; seek medical advice for later fever, rash, headache, weakness, or joint pain.
